title: 10 Best Custom Dashboard Software for 2026
summary: Choose dashboard software based on whether users only read data or need to act on it; compares BI, write-back, monitoring, and portal tools.
body_markdown:
**If you need more than charts, this list matters.** I’d split these 10 tools into four groups fast: **write-back apps** ([Jet Admin](https://jetadmin.io/) , UI Bakery, Softr), **BI/reporting** (Power BI,[Tableau](https://www.tableau.com/) ,[Metabase](https://www.metabase.com/) ,[Domo](https://www.domo.com/) ,[Zoho Analytics](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/) ), **monitoring** ([Grafana](https://grafana.com/) ), and **Google-based reporting** ([Looker Studio](https://lookerstudio.google.com/) ).


Here’s the short answer: if you need users to **view and change data** , Jet Admin and UI Bakery stand out. If you need **analysis and reporting** , Power BI and Tableau are the main picks. If you need **system dashboards** , Grafana fits best. If you want a **free report builder** , Looker Studio is the low-cost option. And if your team already uses Zoho or spreadsheets, **Zoho Analytics** and **Softr** are easier to place.


The article compares each tool on the six points that matter most:


- **Data connections**
- **How much you can customize**
- **Role-based access**
- **SSO and audit logs**
- **Cloud vs. self-hosted**
- **Pricing**


It also reflects a bigger shift in software buying.[Gartner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gartner) says **70% of new enterprise apps will use[low-code or no-code tools](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/low-code-platform-from-ai-prompt-to-production-grade-apps/) by 2026** . That helps explain why tools like Jet Admin, Softr, and UI Bakery are getting more attention.


If I had to narrow the list fast, I’d use this cheat sheet:


- **Jet Admin:** best for[internal apps, admin panels,](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/php-admin-panel-architecture-options-and-how-to-build-one-that-lasts/) and direct database write-back
- **[Microsoft Power BI](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-bi) :** best for Microsoft-based BI and data modeling
- **Tableau:** best for interactive analysis and data visualization
- **Metabase:** best for simple self-service reporting
- **Grafana:** best for live system monitoring
- **Looker Studio:** best for free Google-based reporting
- **Zoho Analytics:** best for teams already using Zoho
- **Domo:** best for large-team dashboard governance
- **Softr:** best for client portals and spreadsheet-based apps
- **UI Bakery:** best for admin panels with more control over logic and layout

## 1.[Jet Admin](https://jetadmin.io/)


Jet Admin is an AI-powered app builder for internal tools, admin panels, and custom dashboards built on top of existing data. It scored **8.7/10** on iTechGuides and ranked **#5 out of 26[internal tool builders for 2026](https://www.jetadmin.io/use-cases/internal-tool-builder)** . For teams that need live data, user permissions, and workflow logic in one place, Jet Admin is a solid option.


### Data connectivity


Jet Admin connects to **200+ integrations** , including Postgres, MySQL, MongoDB,[Supabase](https://supabase.com/) ,[Firebase](https://firebase.google.com/) , REST APIs, Google Sheets, and[Airtable](https://www.airtable.com/) . It also supports native SQL and API access with real-time read and write access.


That means teams can build dashboards directly on production data instead of working around exports, sync delays, or copy-paste workflows.


### Customization and workflows


The platform comes with a drag-and-drop builder, plus support for custom JavaScript and HTML when teams need more control. One feature that stands out is **Figma import** , which lets teams bring dashboard designs straight into Jet Admin and cut down design-to-dev time.


Jet Admin also includes built-in workflow and automation tools for things like approval flows and ticket queues. So it’s not just about showing data. It can help move work forward by allowing teams to[build and ship custom tools](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/custom-business-software-how-to-design-build-and-ship-tools-that-actually-match-your-operations/) that match their specific operations.


### Security and governance


Jet Admin includes role-based access control (RBAC), SSO, SAML, audit logs, and built-in authentication, including magic link and Google login. It also supports row-level permissions, which gives teams tighter control over what each user can view and change.


For companies handling sensitive internal data, that level of control matters a lot.


### Deployment and pricing


Jet Admin is available in **cloud, self-hosted, and on-premise** deployment models, including air-gapped environments. That gives teams more say in how and where the platform runs.


Paid plans start at **$16/month** , billed annually. The Business plan costs about **$48/user/month** .


Here’s the short version: the main tradeoffs come down to customization depth, deployment control, and pricing.

## 2.[Microsoft Power BI](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-bi)


### Customization and workflows


Power BI works best for governed reporting, data modeling, and interactive dashboards inside Microsoft environments. If your team already lives in Microsoft tools, it tends to fit in without much friction.


It supports rich visuals, DAX-based data modeling, and drill-through report interactivity. That makes it a strong pick for analytics teams that need to slice data, trace patterns, and build reports people can click through instead of just read.


Where Power BI shines is reporting. Where it starts to fall short is workflow actions or task-driven internal apps. So the tradeoff is pretty simple: if reporting matters more than app-like workflows, Power BI makes a lot of sense. If your team needs people to *do* things inside the tool, not just analyze data, it may feel limiting.


## 3.[Tableau](https://www.tableau.com/)


Tableau is a BI and data visualization platform built for analytics teams that need interactive dashboards and reports. It’s a strong fit when the main job is analysis and reporting, not building internal tools that people use to update records or move work forward.


### Data connectivity


Tableau connects to a wide mix of data sources, including databases, cloud warehouses, and spreadsheets. That makes it easier for teams to pull reporting into one place instead of jumping between systems.


### Customization and workflows


It supports drill-down views and embedded analytics, which is great when users want to explore the numbers from different angles. But it doesn’t handle forms, record edits, or task workflows. So if people need to inspect data, Tableau fits well. If they need to change records or run a process, it’s not the right tool.


### Security and governance


Tableau supports SSO, role-based access control, and governance features. It also gives teams two deployment paths: Tableau Server for self-hosted deployment and Tableau Cloud for cloud deployment.


### Deployment and pricing fit


Licensing costs, plus Tableau Server infrastructure, can make Tableau expensive for smaller teams. That’s especially true for dashboard-only use cases, where the spend may feel heavy for what you need.

## 4.[Metabase](https://www.metabase.com/)


If your team just needs reporting, Metabase keeps things simple. It’s a BI tool built for self-service reporting on top of databases you already use.


### Data connectivity


Metabase connects straight to your existing data sources, functioning as a[SQL GUI](https://www.jetadmin.io/use-cases/sql-gui) for your databases. It supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server,[BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery) , and[Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/) . It also works with MongoDB for NoSQL data.


### Customization and workflows


Its visual query builder lets people filter, group, and visualize data without writing code. That makes it a solid fit for reporting and light exploration.


What it *doesn’t* do is just as important: Metabase doesn’t support record edits or workflow actions. So if someone on your team needs to update data from a dashboard or kick off a process, Metabase isn’t built for that job.


Capability Metabase


Self-service reporting ✅ Strong


Database connectivity ✅ PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, BigQuery, Snowflake, MongoDB


Operational workflows ❌ Not supported


Metabase works best for read-only reporting. It’s not a fit for dashboards that need to write back to records or run business processes. If your dashboard needs to trigger work or update data, you’ll want[custom dashboard software for secure operations](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/custom-dashboard-software-for-secure-operations-grade-apps/) .


## 5.[Grafana](https://grafana.com/)


Grafana changes the comparison a bit. It leans toward monitoring-first dashboards, not business reporting. In plain English: Grafana was built for teams that need to watch systems, metrics, and status in real time, not for people working through interactive business tasks.


### Data connectivity


Grafana connects to existing data sources, including SQL databases and APIs.


That makes it a solid fit if your data already lives across a few systems and you want to pull it into one place for visibility.


### [customization and workflows](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/custom-dashboard-software-for-secure-operations-grade-apps/amp/)


Grafana dashboards are read-only; they do not support forms, record updates, or workflow actions.


That’s a big line in the sand. You can view what’s happening, but you can’t use the dashboard itself to submit data, change records, or kick off a process. So if your team needs dashboards that double as working tools, Grafana won’t be the right match.


### Security and governance


Grafana includes role-based access control, SSO, and audit logs, which help teams share dashboards securely.


So while it’s read-only from a workflow angle, it still gives teams solid control over who can see what and how access is managed.


### Deployment and pricing fit


Grafana supports self-hosted deployment.


Grafana is the right tool when your team is focused on live monitoring and read-only status views. For daily business reporting or operational dashboards, it sits outside its core strength.


## 6.[Looker Studio](https://lookerstudio.google.com/)


Looker Studio is a good fit if you want **free reporting that works well with Google tools** . Its main draws are simple setup, direct Google access, and **$0 pricing** .


It connects natively to Google products and to third-party sources through connectors. But there’s a catch: it uses **scheduled refreshes** , not live connections. So if you need data the second it changes, this may feel a bit limiting.


Charts and filters are **read-only** . That means people can interact with what they see, but they can’t push data back or use two-way workflows. It’s also **cloud-only (SaaS)** , and sharing runs through Google account permissions.

## 7.[Zoho Analytics](https://www.zoho.com/analytics/)


Zoho Analytics is a solid fit for teams already working inside **Zoho CRM** , **Zoho Books** , or **Zoho Projects** and looking for reporting, embedded dashboards, and AI-assisted analysis. It makes the most sense when your reporting stays close to the day-to-day data already living in the Zoho ecosystem.


### Data connectivity


Zoho Analytics connects to SQL databases, cloud apps, spreadsheets, CSV files, and APIs. It also comes with native connectors across the Zoho product suite, which makes setup smoother if you're already all-in on Zoho.


That said, many setups need data to be pulled into a central dataset or warehouse before reporting starts. So while it handles data from many sources, there's still an extra step if you want reporting on live operational data. Because of that, it's not the best match for[custom dashboard software](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/untitled-16/) for real-time internal tools that sit right on top of source systems.


### Customization and workflows


You can build dashboards with drag-and-drop components, add filters, and show different views based on user role. If you want reports to appear inside other apps, embedded analytics is available. Workflow automation also helps turn report-based tasks into follow-up actions.


But here's the line Zoho Analytics draws: it stays focused on reporting. It doesn't lean into forms, buttons, or write-back actions.


### Security and governance


Zoho Analytics supports **RBAC** and **SSO** , which covers standard governance needs.


### Deployment and pricing fit


Zoho Analytics is cloud-hosted by default, so it's a good fit for teams that want a managed setup without dealing with infrastructure. Pricing goes up as user count and data volume grow.


Factor Zoho Analytics


**Best Data Sources** Zoho apps, SQL databases, spreadsheets and CSV files, APIs


**Live Query Support** Requires data ingestion or centralization first


**Deployment** Cloud-hosted


**Pricing** Rises with users and data volume


**Best For** Reporting-focused teams already using Zoho


For teams that need broader enterprise analytics, the next option moves past ecosystem-based reporting and into larger-scale dashboarding.


## 8.[Domo](https://www.domo.com/)


If the last option leans more toward reporting, Domo moves into **enterprise-scale dashboarding and governance** .


Domo is an enterprise dashboard platform built for teams that need **centralized reporting** , governed access, and broad data connectivity at scale. It does a solid job with cross-source dashboards, supports shared access across large teams, and gives organizations one place to manage reporting across departments. That said, it’s not the best fit for lightweight internal tools or workflows that need frequent write-back actions.


Factor Domo


**Best For** Enterprise teams that need governed, cross-functional dashboards and centralized reporting


**Data Connectivity** Broad, supports multiple data sources across the organization


**Governance** Role-based access control and centralized data management


**Limitations** Not built for write-back workflows or lightweight internal tooling


If your team wants a simpler, lighter dashboard builder, the[best internal tool builder platforms](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/untitled-3/) are easier to pick up.


## 9. Softr


Softr is a no-code/low-code builder for dashboards, internal tools, and client portals. It has a **4.8/5 rating on[G2](https://www.g2.com/)** based on **426 reviews** .


### Data connectivity


Softr connects to **21+ external data sources** , including Airtable, Google Sheets,[Notion](https://www.notion.com/) ,[HubSpot](https://www.hubspot.com/) ,[monday.com](https://monday.com/) , Supabase, and SQL databases like PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, and MariaDB. It also comes with its own relational database, **Softr Databases** , plus **two-way real-time sync** with Airtable and Google Sheets. That’s a big help if your team already runs on spreadsheets and wants to get a dashboard live without moving data into a new system first.


### Customization and workflows


The builder includes blocks for **tables, kanbans, charts, forms, and calendars** . Softr also offers **AI Co-Builder** , which can generate app structure, schemas, and permissions from plain-language prompts. On top of that, **AI-generated UI blocks** give you more room to shape the app the way you want. For automations, **Softr Workflows** can run from UI actions or data changes.


### Security and governance


On the security side, Softr is **SOC 2 Type II certified** and **GDPR compliant** . It supports **RBAC** with **row-level restrictions** , which matters when different users should only see certain records. **SSO** is also available on the **Enterprise** plan.


### Deployment and pricing fit


Softr is cloud-native and fits best for **internal tools, business operations, and client portals** . Pricing starts at **$0/month** . The **Business** plan costs **$329/month** and includes SQL database integration. **Enterprise** pricing is custom and adds **SSO, dedicated SLAs, and success managers** .


Softr makes the most sense when speed and governed access matter more than custom engineering. If your team wants deeper control over layout and workflow logic, the next option goes further.


## 10. UI Bakery


UI Bakery is a solid pick for teams building internal dashboards and admin panels on top of existing databases and APIs. It has a **4.7/5 G2 rating** and an **8.4/10 iTechGuides score** .


It tends to work better for **operational dashboards and admin panels** than for reporting-only setups.


### Data connectivity


UI Bakery connects to **databases** and **REST/GraphQL APIs** . It also supports **Git-based version control** , which helps teams keep changes organized and easier to track.


### Customization and workflows


The drag-and-drop canvas is responsive by default, and it gives you **fine-grained layout controls** for mobile layouts. That means you don't have to fight the editor every time you want a screen to look right on a phone.


Its workflow builder goes past basic triggers. You can set up **multi-step actions with branching logic** and add custom JavaScript when the visual editor hits a wall. In plain English: you can start with no-code, then drop into code when the app needs more than point-and-click rules.


The **AI agent** can generate an app from a plain-language description and then keep working on it by modifying, fixing, extending, and debugging the app. A good way to use it is to let AI scaffold the first version, then tune the logic by hand.


### Security and governance


UI Bakery includes **predefined roles** like admin, editor, and user. It also supports **custom roles with granular permissions** at both the app and data levels.


**SSO** is available on the **Enterprise** plan. That said, teams that want a fully open-source stack may see this as a drawback, and some advanced enterprise governance features need sales review.

## How to Choose the Right Custom Dashboard Software


Start with the main job you need the tool to do.


If your team needs to **read and write data in a production database** , Jet Admin is built for that. If your goal is **BI-style reporting and advanced visualization** , Microsoft Power BI or Tableau are stronger picks. For **real-time infrastructure monitoring** , Grafana is the specialized option. If your data lives in a spreadsheet and you need a **client portal** , Softr is a strong fit.


If that still doesn’t settle it, look at two things: **where your data lives** and **how technical your team is** .


If your data sits in a production database that you can’t move, it makes sense to use a tool that works directly on top of that database, like Jet Admin. If your team is comfortable writing code, Metabase or UI Bakery will likely feel like a natural match. If you need to move fast without code, put Softr or Jet Admin at the top of the list.


Use the summary below only when you’re choosing between close options:


- **[Admin panels and write-back workflows](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/php-admin-panel-architecture-options-and-how-to-build-one-that-lasts/amp/) :** Jet Admin and UI Bakery are best for forms, buttons, and direct database access.
- **Reporting and BI:** Power BI, Tableau, Metabase, and Domo are better for deep analytics and governed reporting.
- **Monitoring:** Grafana is the right call for infrastructure and real-time system visibility.
- **Client portals and no-code apps:** Softr is the fastest path when speed and governed access matter more than custom engineering.
- **Strict security requirements:** Jet Admin, Power BI, Tableau, and Domo offer strong RBAC, SSO/SAML, and audit logs. If you need self-hosting in regulated industries, Jet Admin, Metabase, Grafana, and UI Bakery are the strongest options.


Before you choose, check each vendor’s current docs for pricing, deployment options, SSO, audit logs, and self-hosting details.


## FAQs


### How do I choose between BI and write-back tools?


Choose based on whether you need **historical analysis** or **day-to-day execution** .


Use a BI platform when you need deep historical modeling, complex analysis, and executive reporting. It’s the right fit for looking back, spotting patterns, and helping leaders make sense of the numbers.


Use a write-back tool when teams need to run daily work, trigger workflows, or update data directly in their systems. That’s less about studying what happened and more about moving work forward in the moment.


### When does self-hosting matter for dashboards?


Self-hosting matters when an organization has strict data residency rules, network isolation needs, or regulatory compliance demands. It gives teams full control over their data, so sensitive information doesn’t pass through a vendor’s cloud servers.


For regulated workloads, that can mean tighter security and better governance. But there’s a trade-off: teams also need to look at total cost of ownership, including infrastructure, plus the internal DevOps work needed for patches, upgrades, and security hardening.


### What security features should I check before buying?


Check whether the platform supports **least-privilege access** through granular **RBAC** , **SSO** with **SAML/SCIM** , and audit logs that show who viewed or changed dashboards and settings.


You should also review network and security controls, secure credential storage with rotation, and whether **self-hosted** or **hybrid deployment** options are offered. It’s also worth checking if the vendor supports **staging/production separation** .


Confirm each of these points in the vendor’s current documentation.
